text:
elaine: Quick proposal: shrink ingress lifecycle to three canonical phases so our tests and postmortems are easier. Proposal sketch below.

 tom: interested. what are the three phases?

 elaine: ACCEPTED -> STREAMING -> TERMINAL. Terminal has a typed reason, e.g. OK / UPSTREAM_ERR / CLIENT_ABORT / TIMEOUT / RATE_LIMIT.

 vik: Love the simplicity. How do we signal transient states like queueing/backpressure?

 elaine: Admission attributes on ACCEPTED: `x-rw-admit: ok|queued|reject` and optional `x-rw-queue-eta`. STREAMING can carry `x-rw-pressure: low|med|high` as a hint. These are attributes, not lifecycle states.

 frank: Retries are the big footgun. Current mid-stream resume logic caused most dupes. Suggest: allow automatic retry only before any body bytes; after first byte, request becomes non-retriable unless `x-rw-resume=true` was explicit and server supports resume.

 tom: so clients opt-in to resumable semantics. good. Also define an idempotency header `x-rw-idempotency-key` for safe server-side dedupe.

 vik: trailers are messy across SDKs. Can we standardize a minimal trailer contract? e.g. trailer `x-rw-final: <OK|UPSTREAM_ERR|CLIENT_ABORT|TIMEOUT|RATE_LIMIT>` and optional `x-rw-final-code`. limit to 256 bytes.

 elaine: yes. edge must preserve and forward trailers even for chunked streams; implement size cap to keep memory bounded. If trailer absent, fall back to connection close reason.

 frank: observability: emit one event per phase transition. Add span tags `rw.phase` and `rw.terminal_reason`. Also increment a small `rw.checkpoint` counter on major events to map partial progress in traces. Keep metrics cardinality low.

 tom: draining and deploy behavior?

 elaine: ACCEPTED can happen while node draining, but add `x-rw-node-state=draining` and prefer fast-fail of new accepts when SLOs can't be met. Fast-fail returns 503 + `Retry-After`.

 vik: compatibility plan?

 elaine: edge shim that maps old phases -> new phases for 90 days, emit deprecation logs, SDK compatibility checklist (node/go/python) and a small compatibility library that ensures trailers are surfaced to clients.

 frank: security note: trust `x-rw-` headers only when they come from our frontdoor; strip/ignore client-supplied values downstream.

 ci-bot: Created task ENG-6882 to run sdk trailer checks and ENG-6883 to add shim (https://issues/redwood/ENG-6882, ENG-6883).

 elaine: action items: tom -> draft RFC with simple diagram and enums; vik -> run trailer-compat across SDKs; frank -> metric names and low-cardinality label plan. If all good, quick RFC sync next week.

 tom: I'll start the RFC and include short code snippets for node/python showing `x-rw-idempotency-key` and `x-rw-resume=true`.

 vik: I'll post SDK matrix results here.

 elaine: thanks team.
